explanation.text:
Your product is likely to meet the AfCFTA rules of origin.

Main reasons:
- One imported ingredient is in heading 19.01: Cereal-based premix preparation, value GHS 3,600.00. This is 6% of the ex-works price of GHS 60,000.00. The limit is 15%.
- These steps in Ghana are more than simple operations: roasting of millet and soya, cooking by extrusion and drum drying of the cooked paste.

Note: the 15% limit is the AfCFTA tolerance rule (EX.CL/1329(XL), Annex, item 3). Your margin is 9 percentage points. A change in prices or recipe can change the result.

What to do next:
- Keep your supplier declarations, invoices and production records together.
- You decide whether to apply. GRA Customs and the National AfCFTA Approval Committee make the official decision.

expected.derivation: Imported premix (heading 19.01) GHS 3,600.00 / ex-works GHS 60,000.00 = 6.0% ≤ 15%. Millet from Burkina Faso is Chapter 10, not heading 19.01, so cumulation is not needed. Expected only if every value is read correctly.
